original.text: प्रवृत्ते भैरवीचक्रे सर्वे वर्णा द्विजातयः । निवृत्ते भैरवीचक्रे सर्वे वर्णाः पृथक् पृथक् ॥ स्त्री वाथ पुरुषः षण्डश्चण्डालो वा द्विजोत्तमः । चक्रेऽस्मिन्नैव भेदोऽस्ति सर्वे शिवसमाः स्मृताः ॥

paraphrase: The yogin who knows the highest is free of attachment, beyond adjuncts and residual impressions, immersed in his own nature. The body is the temple, the jīva is the God Sadāśiva; he should cast off ignorance like stale offerings and worship with the sense 'I am He'. The jīva is Śiva and Śiva is the jīva; the jīva is purely Śiva: bound by fetters it is called jīva, freed from them it is Sadāśiva — as rice in its husk is paddy and without the husk is grain; bound by karma one is jīva, freed from karma, Sadāśiva.

paraphrase: The Kula path taught by Bhairava treats as high what the world holds low and as low what it holds high; for the Kaulas misconduct is right conduct, the forbidden is to be done, the undrinkable drinkable; for them there is no injunction or prohibition, no merit or sin, no heaven or hell.
